`devin/p32-8-memory-concurrency-and-recovery` · run
`implement-spec spec=docs/tickets/168_P32.8__memory-concurrency-and-recovery.md live_verification=false`
(full rigor) · BUILD_INDEX row 168 · stream **S6** — Round 10.

## Summary

Interrupted closeout now resumes to **exactly one** closeout — never a duplicated index
row, a second PR, or invented closure — and two worktrees can validate concurrently
without overwriting each other's report.

- **`closeout-op/1`** (`docs/build/tools/closeout_protocol.py` — stdlib, journaled under
  the shared git common dir so every worktree of one clone sees one journal):
  - **pre-PR operation id** `co-<sha256[16]>` over `(schema, ticket_id, attempt,
    implementation, base)` — defined before any remote PR creation; same identity at any
    boundary is an idempotent resume;
  - **four expected-state preconditions** (`expected_next_ticket`,
    `expected_last_completed`, `expected_control_digest` over LEDGER+BUILD_INDEX+DEFERRALS,
    `expected_chain_head`) compared against the **authoritative chain ref** (the main
    worktree of the shared common dir — never the caller's stale files); any mismatch
    exits 2 naming deltas and writes nothing — no partial advancement;
  - **scoped advisory lock** — `mkdir`-atomic, keyed to the stable chain id + common dir
    + repo-relative ledger path; **documented single-host assumption** (PID liveness is
    meaningful only on the recorded host; foreign-host locks are refused with
    instructions, never reclaimed here); a stale lock is surfaced with recovery
    instructions and reclaimed only via `--recover-stale` after a confirmed-dead PID —
    never removed merely because time elapsed; every recovery is appended to
    `recoveries.jsonl`;
  - **state machine** `prepared → external-known → memory-committed → acknowledged`
    (+ `aborted`/`superseded` terminal side-states): a different implementation identity
    on an in-flight or closed ticket is refused unless a new **recorded** attempt
    (`--attempt N --reason`) explains it; a second PR number for one operation is the
    duplicate-creation failure mode — refused; ambiguous remote creation is reconciled by
    exact head/base before retry (`--uncertain`; a *failed* lookup is inconclusive, never
    "safe to create"); next dispatch is prohibited before `acknowledge` sees the
    authoritative advance (`lastCompleted` = ticket, `nextTicket` moved on);
  - **the validated git commit IS the memory transaction** — `memory-committed` requires
    the commit to exist, descend from `expected_chain_head`, CAS-match its parent's
    control digest against the recorded expected digest, touch LEDGER + BUILD_INDEX, and
    pass the validator. Uncommitted file replacement is never a transition;
  - **`activation-check`** refuses cutover (exit 6) while any legacy/event divergence
    exists — a DEFERRALS row without an anchor (legacy-only), an event for an unknown
    obligation (event-only), or a cell disagreeing with its event-chain head — consumed
    from P32.7's `obligation_events.py`, never forked.
- **Validator local patch** (`scripts/docs/check-build-memory.sh`, marked **NO LONGER
  byte-identical** — truthful vendoring provenance): JSON report → caller-selected
  `--json PATH` or a unique per-run `mktemp` file (the shared
  `/tmp/build-memory-check.json` write-collision is removed; atomic temp+mv write);
  `build-memory-check/2` records checked-input identity
  `{repo, commit, dirty, input_digest}` (sha256-chained over every file read — a report
  is valid only for the revision it names); diagnostics carry
  `{check, severity, file, obligation, evidence, message}` and `summary.exit` agrees with
  the process exit code. Detection logic unchanged. `Makefile` + the planning
  `check_memory_isolated.py` wrapper now pass `--json` (the wrapper no longer patches a
  private copy).
- **Reviewed entry-point patch contract** (`CLOSEOUT_WRITER_PROTOCOL.md` §"contract/
  patch/1..3"): implement-spec closeout boundary, orchestrator repair + worker dispatch,
  and the upstream validator delta — documented for operator application at the
  D-R10-MEMORY-1 cutover; no user-global skill file is edited from this repository.
- **ADR-127** + Appendix F row + ADR index + BL-058 sources; `COVERAGE_MATRIX`
  SIG-MEM-003 → MET (implementation/fixture domains); `docs/build/README.md` tool index +
  v2.1 changelog.
